mbm-0668.clue: I count the foxtrot on my cuff.
mbm-0668.quote: My first teacher stitched three tiny buttons into my practice cuff. I'd tap a button for each slow step while I waited my turn. They're still there on opening night.

mbm-0669.clue: I play bass by the aquarium.
mbm-0669.quote: Our band rehearses at a pet shop after closing. Whenever I play the low note, the angelfish come out from behind their castle. I like to think we have regulars already.

mbm-0670.clue: I never wash the old belt into a knot.
mbm-0670.quote: At my first judo competition I tied such a hopeful knot my coach had to undo it with a spoon handle. My hands shake less these days. The spoon stayed in his coaching bag.

mbm-0671.clue: I didn't know we swam in different blues.
mbm-0671.quote: My teammate wore tinted goggles and I borrowed them for one length. Our gray indoor pool turned bright turquoise. The clear lenses surprised my teammate just as much.

mbm-0672.clue: I make room for the scruffy daisy.
mbm-0672.quote: The last flower in every bunch drooped straight over the rim. I threw a squat vase and pierced the shoulder with little holes for a second tier. Our shortest daisies now sit at the grown-ups' table.

mbm-0673.clue: I built a robot with a bad knee.
mbm-0673.quote: I lost one cap from a mecha knee joint and cut a new one from a green pen lid. The repair looks so convincing the club asked for its battle story. I'm still inventing one.

mbm-0674.clue: I collect the seats nobody picks.
mbm-0674.quote: I've watched films from the first row, beside the exit, directly under the balcony clock. My favorite is the lonely seat tucked into the curve of the old cinema wall. It's like having a private box.

mbm-0675.clue: I paint tiny portraits of the lunch counter.
mbm-0675.quote: I asked each cook to lend me one utensil. The picture has five spoons and a bent whisk in it. You'd be surprised how easily they recognized one another.

mbm-0676.clue: I run the block with the wind chimes.
mbm-0676.quote: On breezy days that street does my pacing for me. One morning all the chimes went quiet right as I passed. I gave the last set a little bow and kept running.

mbm-0677.clue: I ski the turn with the blue view.
mbm-0677.quote: There's one curve where the lake comes into sight below the slope. My instructor had to call me back the first time I saw it. Now I stop at the side and take my look properly.

mbm-0678.clue: I programmed a mouse for my uncle.
mbm-0678.quote: He has a shop cat who couldn't care less about string. My pixel mouse darted across the monitor once and the cat sat up straight. I haven't had a software review that good since.

mbm-0679.clue: I hear that hollow domino before I see it.
mbm-0679.quote: One domino in my set has a hollow knock. My uncle played it, and our whole table grinned before looking down. We know that knock the way we know his laugh.

mbm-0680.clue: I juggle the pears before they're ripe.
mbm-0680.quote: Hard pears can stand a little indignity. The ripe ones go straight into a tart. My housemates now ask whether supper is still in rehearsal or ready for the oven.

mbm-0681.clue: I trained for the dumpling table.
mbm-0681.quote: Each station at the fair had a different filling. I only meant to enter the potato round. Six dumplings later the judge announced I'd qualified for dessert, and my family produced a second fork.

mbm-0682.clue: I keep the nick in my drumstick.
mbm-0682.quote: Our first gig was in a room so small my stick caught the lampshade during the fill. The lamp survived. The nick tells me which way round to hold that stick in the dark.

mbm-0683.clue: I patched the band's cracked tambourine.
mbm-0683.quote: Brown tape looked miserable under stage light. I used a strip from an old silver raincoat instead. At our next show the singer borrowed it and got spotlighted before she sang a note.

mbm-0684.clue: I put the river along the quilt seam.
mbm-0684.quote: I made a quilt map of our campsite and cut the river too wide. My friend said it looked exactly right for the year we flooded. I stitched our tent halfway up the hill.

mbm-0685.clue: I paint the quiet side of the market.
mbm-0685.quote: The fish seller stacks his empty blue crates in the alley. At closing they catch the pink light from the awning. I sold that painting to the man who'd spent all day emptying them.

mbm-0686.clue: I shop with one empty coat pocket.
mbm-0686.quote: The rule is that my market find has to fit in it. Last Saturday I came home with a porcelain lemon. This Saturday I'm leaving the pocket empty until I find it a saucer.

mbm-0687.clue: I paint reflections in a spoon.
mbm-0687.quote: I set a tablespoon upright in a jar and paint the room bent round its curve. My friend's portrait got enormous ears. He bought it before I could make the corrections.

mbm-0688.clue: I stole the baker's victory condition.
mbm-0688.quote: At our board-game table the winner usually gets the crown. My friend bakes a tiny loaf for whoever builds the first mill. Everyone's been fighting over the mill ever since.

mbm-0689.clue: I ride for the sign at the summit.
mbm-0689.quote: The little road sign at the top of our cycling tour has a bent corner. I hang my helmet on that corner while I eat an orange. Now every summit feels like it ought to come with a hook.

mbm-0690.clue: I tour a city by its staircases.
mbm-0690.quote: A guide pointed me toward the cathedral. I got sidetracked by a flight of blue-tiled steps and met a woman carrying flowers up to her shop. I remember every blue step and her enormous daisies.

mbm-0691.clue: I count our raft crew with oranges.
mbm-0691.quote: An orange goes in the dry bag for each paddler. At the takeout I pass them around. One day our guide brought a friend and we shared the last one in eight impossibly skinny smiles.

mbm-0692.clue: I flatten my arepas between two blue plates.
mbm-0692.quote: My grandmother shaped hers in her palms. Mine kept ending up lopsided, so she slid two plates across the counter. Now the faint blue rim on her old china makes me hungry before I start.
